Ford Analyzed Model Year 2021 Mustang Mach-E Batteries, Most Retain More Than 90% Battery Health
22 photos
Photo: Ford
According to Dearborn's favorite son, more than 2,000 customers have driven their 2021 model year Mustang Mach-E crossovers beyond 100,000 miles (approximately 160,000 kilometers) while retaining more than 91 percent of their usable capacity. Another group of more than 30 vehicles has crossed 200,000 miles (over 320,000 kilometers), averaging 88 percent battery health.
To come up with these figures, Ford examined more than 36,000 vehicles produced for the 2021 model year. Said zero-emission crossovers were sold to both retail and fleet customers in the United States and Canada. The Dearborn-based automaker says that more than 2 billion miles (3.2 billion kilometers) have been accumulated by said vehicles thus far.
The average ownership period sits at 5.2 years, and the fleet retains an average of 92 percent of its original usable battery capacities. 95 percent of analyzed Mustang Mach-Es fall between 87 and 97 percent battery health, with Ford obtaining this information through aggregated connected vehicle data rather than lab tests.
One David Blenkle has exceeded 400,000 miles (over 640,000 kilometers) on the original battery in his Mustang Mach-E, yet his vehicle is a 2022 model that does not belong to the study's population. Based on Ford's internal validation data, these NCM batteries are designed to last 10 years at the very least, with 90 percent battery health at the 100,000-mile mark.
In the Mustang Mach-E's first model year, the second-largest manufacturer among Detroit's Big Three offered nickel-cobalt-manganese packs with either 68 or 88 kilowatt-hours of usable energy. Their gross capacities are listed at 75.7 and 98.7 kilowatt-hours, respectively.
Photo: Ford Both packs could be had with either two- or all-wheel drive. Only the First Edition and the GT received the larger battery with dual-motor AWD by default. Even with all-wheel drive, the Mustang Mach-E is a rear-biased vehicle. That is properly surprising when you remember that its underlying architecture is derived from the front-biased C2 of the Escape, Bronco Sport, and Maverick.
Ford's recommendations for customers who intend to drive their Mustang Mach-E for years to come are pretty sensible. First and foremost, use Level 2 charging for everyday driving. Reserve fast charging on direct current for situations that require it. Preconditioning the vehicle while it's plugged in also matters, and so does avoiding unnecessary exposure to extreme temperatures.
The Blue Oval claims that its wider battery-electric model lineup for North America averages more than 90 percent battery health at 100,000 miles, although that figure comes from a separate 2026 field data study rather than the analyzed 2021 model year Mustang Mach-E vehicle population. For model year 2027, the zero-emission sport utility vehicle offers either 88 or 91 kilowatt-hours of usable capacity.
Select and Premium trims get the lesser battery, while the GT and Rally use the beefier unit. Ford has also improved the Mustang Mach-E for 2027 with a new front electric drive unit that lowers manufacturing costs while delivering the same performance as the old motor. The big news for MY27, however, is the introduction of the Trail Package .
Only available in combination with the Select eAWD, this package should be viewed as a different take on the Rally, complete with increased front and rear ride heights. Prospective customers in the US are expected to receive their Trails in the first quarter of 2027.
